proposals: The National Centre for Financial Education should add to its free learning material a module comparing the 50/30/20 split with save-first budgeting, with Indian worked examples at several income levels and a clear statement that neither is personal advice, so readers meet both rules with the same caveats this post carries.

MoSPI should publish household saving estimates by consumption class from its household surveys, so whether a 20% or a 50%-plus savings rate is realistic at Indian income levels — the question this post says it cannot answer — can be checked against data rather than a FIRE-community benchmark from high-income countries.

MoSPI should publish the household saving rate as a share of disposable, after-tax income alongside its existing national accounts tables, so a national figure exists on the same take-home basis that the 50/30/20 rule and its save-first variant both use.
